currentContext.business: Kirloskar Brothers Limited manufactures fluid management solutions - pumps, valves, turbines, PICO and PAT (a turbine operating in reverse), auto-prime and fire-fighting pumps - together with the services, spares and IoT monitoring that surround them. It serves Building and Construction, Marine, Defence, Nuclear, Water, Irrigation, Power, Oil & Gas, Chemical, pharmaceutical and Retail customers, both directly and through distributors. Manufacture of fluid power equipment accounted for 94.30% of standalone turnover, with sales into 28 States and 8 Union Territories in India and more than 120 countries overseas.

Irrigation: Flood control and pump modernisation solutions
Valves: Valves from 6 mm to 5,000 mm diameter
Building and Construction: Smart Skid Mounted Fire Pump Set
Marine & Defence: Canned motor pumps and advanced pumping systems for naval platforms
Small Pump Business: Self priming, Mini-series and Monobloc pumps
IE4 and IE5 motor energy-efficient pump sets
Customer Service, Spares and Engineered: Service execution across the pumping lifecycle

Declaration of dividend on equity shares for the year ended March 31, 2026 is placed before members as ordinary business at the 106th AGM (31 July 2026, held through VC/OAVM), alongside adoption of the standalone and consolidated financial statements. The only other capital-structure event described is the NCLT-approved merger of step-down subsidiary The Kolhapur Steel Limited into wholly owned subsidiary Karad Projects and Motors Limited, a simplification of the group structure.|BRSR reported on a standalone basis for FY 2025-26 with reasonable assurance obtained from M/s SGS India Private Limited under the SEBI BRSR Core and Non-Core framework for assurance and ESG disclosures for the value chain|Energy management treated as an opportunity - strategising deployment of renewable energy options for cost saving and greening business operations to move towards Net Zero|Climate strategy executed through improving energy efficiency, optimising operational processes, reducing emissions and integrating sustainability considerations into products and technologies|Energy-efficient pumping solutions and sustainable infrastructure applications positioned to support energy optimisation, water efficiency, industrial decarbonisation and climate resilience across customer sectors|Climate risk assessment, transition planning, sustainability targets and governance oversight as the stated approach to climate-transition risk|Waste reduction initiatives across operations, segregation and safe handling of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, recycling, reuse and recovery of materials, strengthening circular economy practices and regular monitoring of waste generation and disposal|EHS management systems, trainings, audits, incident investigation and safety culture as the occupational health and safety framework|Innovation and sustainable product development identified as a material opportunity, focused on high-performance, energy-efficient pumping solutions|Dedicated ESG grievance channel (sustainability@kbl.co.in) within a stakeholder grievance redressal mechanism spanning communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers, suppliers, dealers, governing bodies and financial institutions; open grievances under evaluation are to be resolved in FY 2026-27|Sustainability governance is anchored on a named owner - Head, Corporate Sustainability & Excellence - as the BRSR contact point
currentContext.expansion: KBL describes its expansion in footprint and capability terms rather than as a spending plan. The manufacturing network comprises 9 domestic and 7 overseas manufacturing facilities together with in-house foundries and CII GreenCo certified plants, and manufacturing operations across Kirloskarvadi, Dewas, Kaniyur and Sanand are said to have delivered consistent performance supported by TPM deployment, capacity expansion, product innovation and ESG-focused practices. Capability additions during the year were concentrated at Kirloskarvadi: the ATPD Division obtained ISO 19443:2018 certification from DNV (certificate C724654, valid 26 November 2025 to 25 November 2028) covering ITNS activities for centrifugal pumps and allied components, and the Hydraulic Research Centre Pump Testing Laboratory obtained NABL accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (certificate TC-17726, issued 19 March 2026, valid to 18 March 2030) along with approval from the Hydraulic Institute, USA - positioning it among globally recognised pump testing facilities. The Kirloskarvadi plant also received the TPM Excellence Award from the Japan Institute of Plant Maintenance. Commercially, the report cites orders from Adani Power for large concrete volute pumps for cooling water systems, the engineering and supply of Primary and Secondary Heat Transport Pumps for the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam, an indigenous pumping solution developed for retail petroleum outlets, and an expanded retail footprint through PetroTurbo outlets. Funding intent is conservative: capital expenditure is stated to be funded largely through internal accruals, with focused efforts to minimise debt costs enabling a zero-debt position so that operations and expansion plans can be self-funded. No rupee capex budget, commissioning date or capacity-addition target for a named future project is disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity: climate change can affect operations, supply chain continuity and cost structure through changing regulations, carbon reduction requirements and extreme weather events, implying increased compliance and transition costs; the offsetting opportunity is rising demand for energy-efficient pumping solutions.

Transition to a low-carbon economy may alter customer expectations, regulations and capital allocation. Negative implications flagged are capital expenditure required to transition to low-carbon operations, potential impairment of assets exposed to transition risks, increased compliance costs and potential loss of competitiveness if market expectations are not met. Mitigation is climate risk assessment, transition planning, sustainability targets and governance oversight.

A priority risk given industrial operations: manufacturing processes involving heavy equipment, welding, foundry activities and material handling require stringent safety measures. Negative implications include costs related to incidents, compensation, insurance, legal liabilities, operational downtime and regulatory penalties. Mitigation is EHS management systems, trainings, audits, incident investigation and safety culture.

Risks relate to waste generation and disposal and the associated social and regulatory impacts. Mitigation covers waste reduction initiatives, segregation and safe handling of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, recycling, reuse and recovery, strengthening circular economy practices and regular monitoring of waste generation and disposal.

The Board's Report describes FY 2025-26 as a global environment marked by slowing yet resilient economic growth, elevated energy prices and cautious capital spending - conditions that directly affect demand for capital equipment such as pumps.

risks.risk: Dependence on government-led and infrastructure spending
risks.note: Order momentum is described as coming from government bodies, OEMs and EPC contractors - the Water Resources Department Maharashtra, Kolkata Municipal Corporation, NVDA, the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Uttar Pradesh Irrigation Department - so demand is structurally tied to government-led initiatives, urban infrastructure investment and industrial modernisation programmes.

Manufacture of fluid power equipment accounts for 94.30% of turnover, leaving the entity dependent on one product family, while exports contribute only 7.70% of turnover despite a presence in 120+ countries - concentrating standalone revenue in the Indian market.

Listed among the material topics identified in the report, alongside regulatory compliance and business ethics, as issues the Company tracks; no quantified exposure is disclosed in the routed sections.

one-line thesis: KBL delivered muted FY26 revenue (+1%) due to transient foundry ERP disruptions and Jal Jeevan funding delays, but Q4 momentum (+10%) and a record 30% domestic order book growth signal a strong FY27 rebound driven by nuclear indigenization and data center cooling demand. Margins faced headwinds from one-time labor code costs (Rs. 389mn) and a low-margin product mix in the UK, though management guides for margin recovery as service revenue normalizes.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Q4 Rs. 14.15bn (+10% YoY), FY26 Rs. 45.38bn (+1% YoY); EBITDA: Q4 Rs. 2.09bn (14.8% margin), FY26 Rs. 6.21bn (13.7% margin); PAT: Q4 Rs. 1.12bn, FY26 Rs. 3.77bn (impacted by Rs. 389mn exceptional labor code cost); Order Book: Domestic Rs. 24.68bn (+30% YoY), International Rs. 14.81bn (+21% YoY); Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified in transcript, though dividend of Rs. 7/share declared.
guidance: Revenue: Targeting double-digit growth in FY27; Margin: Expect reversion to FY25 levels as UK service mix improves and foundry stabilizes; Order Inflow: Robust pipeline in Power, Water, Data Centers; Capex/Commissioning: Foundry ERP stabilization complete, focusing on operational efficiency rather than heavy greenfield capex.
order book & pipeline: Total consolidated order book stands at ~Rs. 39.5bn (Domestic Rs. 24.68bn + Intl Rs. 14.81bn). Domestic book grew 30% YoY driven by Building & Construction, Marine/Defense, Oil & Gas, and Power (Coal/Nuclear). International book grew 21% YoY fueled by Oil & Gas, Water utilities, and Data Centers in US/UK.
segment / subsidiary detail: Domestic: Growth in Building/Construction, Defense, Oil & Gas, Power (Thermal/Nuclear), Water/Irrigation. Retail segment hit by Jal Jeevan payment delays. International: US business (Rs. 540cr run-rate) diversified into Fire (35%), Data Centers (25%), and Municipal/Water. UK business faced EBITDA drop (Rs. 95cr to Rs. 58cr) due to high energy prices idling industrial service clients; pivoting to Water (United Utilities framework) and Data Centers.
growth verticals / optionality: Nuclear Power: Indigenous IP for Fast Breeder and Small Modular Reactors (SMR) positions KBL for 100-200 GW nuclear target. Data Centers: High-value cooling/HVAC pump packages ($2mn+ per 1MW facility) with 25% contribution to US revenue already. Defense: Increased government focus on marine and defense pumping systems. Global EPC partnerships: Supplying Siemens, Alstom, Turkish contractors for overseas thermal projects.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 13.7% (vs higher historical levels) due to: 1) One-time Rs. 389mn labor code implementation cost (exceptional item); 2) Foundry ERP transition disruptions affecting small/medium pump dispatch; 3) UK mix shift from high-margin service to lower-margin product sales due to industrial idling from high power prices. Management expects margin recovery in FY27 as service work resumes and foundry efficiencies realize.
capex / expansion: No major greenfield capex announced. Focus on brownfield optimization: Foundry ERP implementation (now stabilized) to improve material accounting and dispatch efficiency. Internal capacity enhancement to hedge against gas shortages for foundry operations.
capital allocation: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 7 per share (350% on Rs. 2 face value) for FY26. Capital prioritized for working capital to support 30% order book growth and R&D for nuclear/data center specialized pumps.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability impacting gas availability and raw material costs (Strait of Hormuz reference). Jal Jeevan Mission funding delays at state level affecting dealer payments and dispatches. UK industrial sector weakness due to high energy prices reducing service demand. Execution risk on large nuclear/data center projects transitioning from prototype to commercial orders.
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic. Acknowledges transient operational headwinds (ERP, Labor Codes, JJM delays) but emphasizes strong order intake, pricing power via efficiency premiums, and strategic positioning in high-growth sectors (Nuclear, Data Centers). Conservative revenue recognition policy highlighted.
non-obvious takeaways: KBL's US entry strategy via fire pumps (low service requirement) allowed distributor penetration where water pumps faced entrenched competition; now leveraging that footprint for high-margin data center cooling. Nuclear pump IP is fully indigenous (designed in India), reducing import dependency for critical atomic energy projects. 10 US states remain completely uncovered, offering latent geographic expansion.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High energy prices in UK idling industrial service clients, shifting mix to lower-margin products | SPP UK Competitors (non-energy intensive focus) | beneficiary | Low | KBL is actively diversifying UK service mix to water/utilities to mitigate this; competitors focused purely on heavy industry may struggle more. |
| Jal Jeevan Mission funding delays causing dispatch bottlenecks for small pump retailers | Small-scale Agricultural Pump Assemblers | loser | Med | KBL's strict credit policy protects cash flow but slows volume; smaller unorganized players may face worse liquidity crunches. |
| Need for specialized cooling pumps for hyperscale data centers | KIRLOSKAR BROTHERS LTD | beneficiary | High | Already secured 25% of US revenue from data centers; indigenous nuclear pump IP creates moat for upcoming SMR tenders. |

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.

hero.oneLiner: A Kirloskar Group engineering company that, over a century, has evolved from India's leading pump manufacturer into a global provider of advanced fluid management solutions spanning pumps, valves and turbines.
hero.industry: Industrial Fluid Dynamics & Critical Infrastructure Pumps

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A Kirloskar Group engineering company that, over a century, has evolved from India's leading pump manufacturer into a global provider of advanced fluid management solutions spanning pumps, valves and turbines.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Kirloskar Brothers Limited manufactures fluid management solutions - pumps, valves, turbines, PICO and PAT (a turbine operating in reverse), auto-prime and fire-fighting pumps - together with the services, spares and IoT monitoring that surround them. It serves Building and Construction, Marine, Defence, Nuclear, Water, Irrigation, Power, Oil & Gas, Chemical, pharmaceutical and Retail customers, both directly and through distributors. Manufacture of fluid power equipment accounted for 94.30% of standalone turnover, with sales into 28 States and 8 Union Territories in India and more than 120 countries overseas.

- Kirloskar Brothers International B.V. (KBIBV) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary in The Netherlands, 100% held; holding entity for the international pump businesses
- Kirloskar Corrocoat Private Limited (KCPL) — subsidiary: Indian entity, 65% held; reported in the BRSR as both subsidiary and joint venture

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Domestic: Growth in Building/Construction, Defense, Oil & Gas, Power (Thermal/Nuclear), Water/Irrigation. Retail segment hit by Jal Jeevan payment delays. International: US business (Rs. 540cr run-rate) diversified into Fire (35%), Data Centers (25%), and Municipal/Water. UK business faced EBITDA drop (Rs. 95cr to Rs. 58cr) due to high energy prices idling industrial service clients; pivoting to Water (United Utilities framework) and Data Centers.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Water Resource Management:** Auto Prime pumps, KirloSmart™ 2.0 IoT solutions, Spares, Solar hybrid pumping systems
- **Irrigation:** Irrigation pumps, Flood control and pump modernisation solutions
- **Valves:** Valves from 6 mm to 5,000 mm diameter, MRO / repeat project supplies
- **Building and Construction:** Smart firefighting and automation solutions, KirloSmart™ Fire, Smart Skid Mounted Fire Pump Set
- **Power and Nuclear:** Concrete Volute Pumps (cooling water systems), Primary Heat Transport Pumps, Secondary Heat Transport Pumps, Concrete Volute Circulating Water Pumps, Firefighting systems
- **Marine & Defence:** Canned motor pumps and advanced pumping systems for naval platforms
- **Industry:** Energy-efficient and special-application pumps
- **Small Pump Business:** Self priming, Mini-series and Monobloc pumps, Submersible pumps with CED-coated components, IE4 and IE5 motor energy-efficient pump sets
- **Digital / Smart Solutions:** KirloSmart™ Nano, KirloSmart™ Fire, KirloSmart™ 2.0
- **Customer Service, Spares and Engineered Services:** Energy audits, Retrofit solutions, Service execution across the pumping lifecycle

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Infrastructure and urban infrastructure
- Water supply, water resource management and sanitation
- Irrigation and agriculture
- Power (including nuclear)
- Process industries - steel, chemicals, coal and mining
- Petrochemicals and Oil & Gas, including retail petroleum outlets
- Marine and Defence
- Building and Construction, including airports and disaster management projects
- Pharmaceutical and Retail
- Domestic India - 28 States and 8 Union Territories
- International - 120+ countries; exports contributed 7.70% of standalone turnover

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:
- ISO 19443:2018 nuclear-specific Quality Management System for the ATPD Division, Kirloskarvadi (DNV Business Assurance, certificate no. C724654, valid 26 November 2025 to 25 November 2028), covering ITNS activities for centrifugal pumps and allied components
- NABL accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 for the Hydraulic Research Centre Pump Testing Laboratory, Kirloskarvadi (certificate TC-17726, issued 19/03/2026, valid until 18/03/2030)
- Approval from the Hydraulic Institute, USA for the Kirloskarvadi pump testing facility
- CII GreenCo certified plants
- BIS and BEE approved energy-efficient pump models (Sanand)
- BRSR assured by M/s SGS India Private Limited - reasonable assurance under the SEBI BRSR Core and Non-Core framework

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Total consolidated order book stands at ~Rs. 39.5bn (Domestic Rs. 24.68bn + Intl Rs. 14.81bn). Domestic book grew 30% YoY driven by Building & Construction, Marine/Defense, Oil & Gas, and Power (Coal/Nuclear). International book grew 21% YoY fueled by Oil & Gas, Water utilities, and Data Centers in US/UK.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue: Targeting double-digit growth in FY27; Margin: Expect reversion to FY25 levels as UK service mix improves and foundry stabilizes; Order Inflow: Robust pipeline in Power, Water, Data Centers; Capex/Commissioning: Foundry ERP stabilization complete, focusing on operational efficiency rather than heavy greenfield capex.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Nuclear Power: Indigenous IP for Fast Breeder and Small Modular Reactors (SMR) positions KBL for 100-200 GW nuclear target. Data Centers: High-value cooling/HVAC pump packages ($2mn+ per 1MW facility) with 25% contribution to US revenue already. Defense: Increased government focus on marine and defense pumping systems. Global EPC partnerships: Supplying Siemens, Alstom, Turkish contractors for overseas thermal projects.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The year unfolded against a challenging global backdrop of geopolitical conflicts, trade realignments, volatile tariff regimes, inflationary pressures and uneven economic recovery, which influenced business sentiment and capital investment decisions
- The core business remained robust despite foreign exchange movements influencing reported results, supported by resilient operating margins and sustained cost and process optimisation initiatives
- The international business, led by the Kirloskar Brothers International B.V. Group, delivered resilient and well-balanced performance with stable margins, consistent underlying growth and disciplined execution
- All KBI BV Group companies reported profitability for the first time since inception, described as validating the strategic direction, governance framework and execution discipline
- The year witnessed slower market conditions across certain sectors, met with a diversified portfolio, manufacturing strength and customer trust
- India's acceleration towards cleaner energy is strengthening engagement with the nuclear power programme
- Products supporting critical infrastructure at key sites including Navi Mumbai, Guwahati and Noida International Airport
- Backed by a strong order backlog and a continued focus on operational excellence, the international business is described as well-positioned for sustained growth in the years ahead
- The Group enters the new financial year with a strong and healthy order backlog, providing positive visibility and confidence
- Orders for Concrete Volute Pumps (CVPs) reinforce capability in large-scale engineered solutions

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 13.7% (vs higher historical levels) due to: 1) One-time Rs. 389mn labor code implementation cost (exceptional item); 2) Foundry ERP transition disruptions affecting small/medium pump dispatch; 3) UK mix shift from high-margin service to lower-margin product sales due to industrial idling from high power prices. Management expects margin recovery in FY27 as service work resumes and foundry efficiencies realize.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 7 per share (350% on Rs. 2 face value) for FY26. Capital prioritized for working capital to support 30% order book growth and R&D for nuclear/data center specialized pumps.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: KBL describes its expansion in footprint and capability terms rather than as a spending plan. The manufacturing network comprises 9 domestic and 7 overseas manufacturing facilities together with in-house foundries and CII GreenCo certified plants, and manufacturing operations across Kirloskarvadi, Dewas, Kaniyur and Sanand are said to have delivered consistent performance supported by TPM deployment, capacity expansion, product innovation and ESG-focused practices. Capability additions during the year were concentrated at Kirloskarvadi: the ATPD Division obtained ISO 19443:2018 certification from DNV (certificate C724654, valid 26 November 2025 to 25 November 2028) covering ITNS activities for centrifugal pumps and allied components, and the Hydraulic Research Centre Pump Testing Laboratory obtained NABL accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (certificate TC-17726, issued 19 March 2026, valid to 18 March 2030) along with approval from the Hydraulic Institute, USA - positioning it among globally recognised pump testing facilities. The Kirloskarvadi plant also received the TPM Excellence Award from the Japan Institute of Plant Maintenance. Commercially, the report cites orders from Adani Power for large concrete volute pumps for cooling water systems, the engineering and supply of Primary and Secondary Heat Transport Pumps for the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam, an indigenous pumping solution developed for retail petroleum outlets, and an expanded retail footprint through PetroTurbo outlets. Funding intent is conservative: capital expenditure is stated to be funded largely through internal accruals, with focused efforts to minimise debt costs enabling a zero-debt position so that operations and expansion plans can be self-funded. No rupee capex budget, commissioning date or capacity-addition target for a named future project is disclosed in the routed sections.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously Optimistic. Acknowledges transient operational headwinds (ERP, Labor Codes, JJM delays) but emphasizes strong order intake, pricing power via efficiency premiums, and strategic positioning in high-growth sectors (Nuclear, Data Centers). Conservative revenue recognition policy highlighted.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Nuclear-grade qualification: ISO 19443 certification of the ATPD Division is described as a differentiator in the nuclear business, backed by supply of Primary and Secondary Heat Transport Pumps for the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam
- Testing and R&D infrastructure: one of Asia's largest hydraulic research centres at Kirloskarvadi, testing pumps at duty conditions up to 5,000 kW, with NABL accreditation and Hydraulic Institute approval
- Backward integration through in-house foundries, including a high pressure moulding line at Dewas, supporting cost leadership
- Breadth of range from 0.37 kW small pumps to 30 MW engineered units and valves up to 5,000 mm diameter, across nine domestic and seven overseas plants
- Technology firsts cited in the report - first company in India to provide pumps with CED-coated components and first submersible pump company in India to do so - plus IE4/IE5 energy-efficient pump sets
- Distribution and installed-base reach across 28 States and 8 Union Territories and more than 120 countries, sold directly and through distributors
- Services annuity: customer service, spares and the Engineered Services Division (energy audits, retrofits) reinforce leadership across the lifecycle of pumping solutions
- Balance-sheet conservatism - a stated zero-debt position with capital expenditure funded largely through internal accruals
- Digital differentiation through the KirloSmart™ family (2.0, Fire, Nano) for remote monitoring and predictive maintenance

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical instability impacting gas availability and raw material costs (Strait of Hormuz reference). Jal Jeevan Mission funding delays at state level affecting dealer payments and dispatches. UK industrial sector weakness due to high energy prices reducing service demand. Execution risk on large nuclear/data center projects transitioning from prototype to commercial orders.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: KBL's US entry strategy via fire pumps (low service requirement) allowed distributor penetration where water pumps faced entrenched competition; now leveraging that footprint for high-margin data center cooling. Nuclear pump IP is fully indigenous (designed in India), reducing import dependency for critical atomic energy projects. 10 US states remain completely uncovered, offering latent geographic expansion.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen participation in India's nuclear power programme as a supplier of high-precision, mission-critical pumping solutions meeting stringent nuclear standards, backed by ISO 19443 certification of the Advanced Technology Product Division
- Consolidate leadership in high-value infrastructure segments, with Concrete Volute Pump orders as evidence of capability in large-scale engineered solutions
- Expand the retail footprint through PetroTurbo outlets to improve accessibility and responsiveness to customers
- Make innovation a strategic priority - the KirloSmart™ 2.0, KirloSmart™ Fire and …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High energy prices in UK idling industrial service clients, shifting mix to lower-margin products | SPP UK Competitors (non-energy intensive focus) | beneficiary | Low | KBL is actively diversifying UK service mix to water/utilities to mitigate this; competitors focused purely on heavy industry may struggle more. |
| Jal Jeevan Mission funding delays causing dispatch bottlenecks for small pump retailers | Small-scale Agricultural Pump Assemblers | loser | Med | KBL's strict credit policy protects cash flow but slows volume; smaller unorganized players may face worse liquidity crunches. |
| Need for specialized cooling pumps for hyperscale data centers | KIRLOSKAR BROTHERS LTD | beneficiary | High | Already secured 25% of US revenue from data centers; indigenous nuclear pump IP creates moat for upcoming SMR tenders. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Merger] TKSL was merged into Karad Projects and Motors Ltd (KPML) with effect from 5th December 2025 per NCLT order dated 3rd November 2025; KPML figures include TKSL from Q3FY25 onwards, which affects comparability of the KPML series.
- [Board] Three independent directors — Mr. Shrinivas V. Dempo, Mr. Shobinder Duggal and Ms. Ramni Nirula — are shown as "Up to May 24, 2026", indicating a simultaneous board refresh.
- [Group structure] Kirloskar Brothers International B.V. (Netherlands, 100%) is the holding company/SPV for all international businesses; Kirloskar Ebara Pumps (45%) is a JV whose share of profit is consolidated, and Kirloskar Corrocoat is 65% held.
- [Order visibility] The deck frames the order book as the revenue-visibility anchor — "Robust Orderbook Implying Strong Revenue Visibility" — and notes pending order book excludes the small pump business, which is made-to-stock and executed from stock in the same month.
- [Recognition] Received the TPM excellence award from JIPM; SPP Pumps was awarded "Manufacturer of the Year" for the 4th consecutive year; the Kirloskarvadi pump testing laboratory achieved NABL accreditation and Hydraulic Institute accreditation.
